Waiting for you
Approved
👷 Worker — marks rocks, logs loads, sets harvest status, logs service hours, jobs and parts, their own My Info.
⭐ Manager — all of that, plus adding/changing/deleting fields, boundaries, bins, equipment and belts, who farms a field, and the bin archive.
🏛️ Executive — all of that, plus Employee Info and this Approve users screen (approve, remove, set Worker/Manager — but can't make or change Executives).
👑 Owner — everything on this farm, including making Executives and other Owners.
🛠️ Web Administrator — Jason Chaplinski, who runs Rock Marker; can reach every farm to help set it up. No one can remove or change this.
Removing someone locks them out right away, on every device they use.

📊 Reports

Truck sizes

Set approximately how many bushels a FULL load of each truck holds. Used to calculate bushels when logging bin activity.
⚖️ Minnesota legal loads (10-ton roads)
10-wheel tandem (3 axles): about 51,000–54,000 lb gross — depends on axle spacing (rear tandem max 34,000 lb).
Hopper-bottom semi (5 axles): 80,000 lb gross.
Bushels you can haul = legal gross − empty truck weight, ÷ lb per bushel (wheat & soybeans 60, corn 56, canola 50, barley 48).Lower on posted roads and during spring load restrictions. Sugarbeets: +10% with a harvest permit until Nov 30. Check your truck’s exact number with MnDOT’s truck weight calculator.

Not connected — this map is only on this device.
Every device already connects to the shared farm automatically — nobody needs to open this screen or paste anything to see the same live map on a new phone or computer. The fields below are only for the rare case of moving this app to a brand-new Firebase project (for example, starting a completely separate farm's map). One person sets up the free Firebase project (~5 minutes, no cost, no credit card):
  1. Go to console.firebase.google.com, sign in, and click "Add project" (name it anything, Analytics can be off).
  2. In the left sidebar, look for Databases & Storage (Firebase has moved this around — if you don't see that exact label, look for anything mentioning "Firestore") → Firestore → Create database → pick a location → start in production mode → Create.
  3. Open the "Rules" tab of Firestore, replace the contents with the rule below, and click Publish:
    rules_version = '2'; service cloud.firestore { match /databases/{database}/documents { match /farms/{farmCode}/{collection}/{docId} { allow read, write: if true; } } }
  4. Go back to your project's main Overview page. You'll see a row of small platform icons (iOS / Android / web) — click the web icon (</>) to add a web app (if you don't see it there, look for an "Add app" button, or the gear icon → Project settings → "Your apps" further down the page). Give it any nickname → Register app → copy the firebaseConfig block shown → paste it above.
  5. Pick a farm code that isn't easy to guess (anyone who has both the code and these settings can see and edit this map) and tap Connect. Text or email the same settings + code to whoever else should share it.

📂 Downloads

Files for the farm to view and download. Anyone can download — adding, replacing, or removing a file needs the admin code.
📱 Install this app
Add it to your Home Screen for quick access, like any other app
💾 Back up the farm
Saves everything — fields for every crop year, field records, rocks, bins & loads, equipment, jobs, parts, soil tests and fertilizer — into one file on this phone or computer. Free: nothing extra is stored online.
Opening a downloaded Word file: Windows blocks macros in files downloaded from the internet by default — that's a Windows/Word security setting, not something this site controls. Before opening it, right-click the downloaded file → Properties → check "Unblock" → OK. Then open it in Word and macros will work normally. (If there's no "Unblock" checkbox, it's already fine to open.)
